hero.title: Bring in
hero.text: Join fifty Windows PCs on VLAN 80 to sbd.test in planned waves: hardened by policy at first boot, managed with Windows LAPS, certified by SBD-SUBCA01, admitted by 802.1X through NPS on SBD-DHCP01, and watched by the logging pipeline. Follow the rollout, explore the dependencies, and keep the evidence.

scene.label: Interactive 3D lesson network showing the fifty Windows PCs on VLAN 80 and SBD-ADMIN-PC01 in front of the core, with the domain controller, SBD-DHCP01, the issuing CA and the event collector they depend on behind it.
scene.completeCaption: Fifty PCs sit in the Workstations OU, hardened by policy, each with its own Windows LAPS password and machine certificate. 802.1X is enforced on the VLAN 80 ports, and every PC reports its security events to the collector.

nodes.name: 50 Windows PCs
nodes.title: 50 Windows PCs · 10.0.80.100–199
nodes.description: SBD-PC01 to SBD-PC50, cloned from one hashed reference image. The three pilots join in lesson 2 and the rest follow in waves in lesson 6, each landing in the Workstations OU with STIG and firewall policy at first boot.

nodes.name: SBD-ADMIN-PC01
nodes.title: SBD-ADMIN-PC01 · 10.0.60.30
nodes.description: The endpoint administration seat on VLAN 60, a virtual machine on SBD-ADMIN-SRV01 built in course 1.8. The workstation firewall policy allows Remote Desktop and remote management only from here, only SBD Tier 2 Admins may read the fleet’s Windows LAPS passwords, and lesson 7 scans the fleet sample from the SCC copy course 1.8 installed there.

nodes.name: SBD-DC01
nodes.title: SBD-DC01 · 10.0.10.10
nodes.description: Holds the Workstations OU, the delegated join account, and the STIG, local Administrators, firewall, DNS registration, LAPS and wired 802.1X policies linked there. It authenticates each join and stores each PC’s managed password and the DNS records SBD-DHCP01 registers; SBD-DC02 holds the same directory and records.

nodes.name: SBD-DHCP01
nodes.title: SBD-DHCP01 · 10.0.20.10
nodes.description: Leases each PC its address from the 10.0.80.100–199 pool through the core’s relay. Lesson 5 adds the Network Policy Server role here for 802.1X port admission only, so the server stays in the member-server tier.

nodes.name: SBD-SUBCA01
nodes.title: SBD-SUBCA01 · 10.0.30.20
nodes.description: The issuing CA. Lesson 4 widens the SBD Computer Authentication template to the SBD Fleet Computers group through the course 1.6 change process; the machine certificates it issues are what 802.1X checks, and its issued log joins the evidence.

nodes.name: SBD-SYSLOG01
nodes.title: SBD-SYSLOG01 · 10.0.20.20
nodes.description: The course 1.10 event collector. It already receives the domain controllers’ events, so the pilot joins arrive on it; lesson 6 enrols the fleet through SBD Event Sources. It forwards what it collects to SBD-SPLUNK01 for analysis.

flows.label: Tier 2 administration · LAPS and SCC scans

stepTitles: Finalize and hash the reference image
Write the naming and wave plan
Delegate the join account and name the PCs’ managers
Link the Windows client STIG policies
Create the firewall and DNS registration GPOs
prepare.mistake: Expecting the core router to block SMB and Remote Desktop between PCs. Traffic inside VLAN 80 never reaches the router, so without the workstation firewall GPO the register’s peer denies are enforced nowhere.
prepare.network: The fifty PCs are planned on VLAN 80, and nothing has joined yet. The Workstations OU on the domain controller already carries the STIG, local Administrators, firewall and DNS registration policy links, below course 1.8’s tier logon GPO, and SBD-ADMIN-PC01 on VLAN 60 is the only management source that policy allows.

control.name: Baseline Configuration
control.body: The hashed reference image and the pre-linked policies are the fleet’s baseline. Record the image version and hash with the GPO links, so every endpoint can be traced back to one documented starting point.
control.question: If an assessor picks one PC at random, which records show that it descends from the approved image and policy set?

checklist: I recorded the reference image version and its SHA256 hash.
I delegated the join account only Create Computer objects on the Workstations OU and made SBD Tier 2 Admins the PCs’ local administrators by GPO.
I confirmed the STIG, firewall and DNS registration GPO links on the Workstations OU, below course 1.8’s tier logon GPO, before any machine joined.

stepTitles: Deploy and join SBD-PC01 to SBD-PC03
Verify OU placement, policy, time, and DNS
Prove the peer and VLAN 60 denies
Find the joins in the logging pipeline
pilot.mistake: Moving a pilot’s computer object into the Workstations OU by hand. If a machine did not land there on its own, the course 1.5 redirect is not working, and the next forty-seven would boot without the hardened policy.
pilot.network: Three pilots on VLAN 80 take leases from SBD-DHCP01 through the core’s relay, join sbd.test and read their policy, and SBD-DHCP01 registers their DNS records. The domain controller’s join events travel to SBD-SYSLOG01 for analysis.

control.name: Configuration Settings
control.body: The pre-linked STIG policies apply the required settings at first boot. gpresult on each pilot shows the settings reached the machine, not just the GPO.
control.question: Which of the pilot checks would catch a machine that joined the domain but never received its policy?

checklist: I joined SBD-PC01 through SBD-PC03 with the delegated account and confirmed each sits in the Workstations OU.
I recorded gpresult, time source and DNS proof for each pilot, and a failed peer SMB test.
I found the three computer-account creations in the analysis searches.

stepTitles: Extend the schema and grant self-update rights
Grant password read access to Tier 2 only
Create the LAPS GPO on the Workstations OU
Retrieve, use, and watch a password rotate
laps.mistake: Granting read access on the managed passwords to a broad group, such as all IT staff. Everyone in it then holds every endpoint’s local administrator secret; the tier model limits reading to SBD Tier 2 Admins.
laps.network: Each pilot now keeps its own rotating local administrator password in the directory. SBD-ADMIN-PC01 retrieves one under the Tier 2 rules and uses it once on a pilot, and the pilot resets it after use.

control.name: Authenticator Management
control.body: Windows LAPS gives every endpoint a unique local administrator password, rotates it on schedule and after use, and stores it encrypted where only SBD Tier 2 Admins (and, by default, Domain Admins) can read it.
control.question: If one endpoint’s local administrator password were captured, what else could an attacker open with it?

checklist: I recorded the schema change as a Tier 0 action performed from AdminJumpBox01.
I confirmed only SBD Tier 2 Admins, beside the default Domain Admins, can read and decrypt the managed passwords.
I retrieved one pilot’s password from SBD-ADMIN-PC01, used it once, and observed the rotation.

stepTitles: Widen the template to a fleet group by change
Add the pilots to the group and watch enrollment
Verify the chain and live revocation
Sample the CA’s issued-certificate log
certificates.mistake: Widening the template’s permission with a quick edit on the CA console, or naming the Workstations OU, which a template permission can’t hold. Skipping the course 1.6 change process leaves no record of who approved fleet enrollment.
certificates.network: The pilots request machine certificates from SBD-SUBCA01 once they are in SBD Fleet Computers, with no one in the loop. Verification fetches the AIA and CDP files from pki.sbd.test over the register’s publication row, F18.

control.name: Public Key Infrastructure Certificates
control.body: Machine certificates come from the approved issuing CA under a documented template, and an endpoint proves the chain to the approved root and live revocation checking before the result is trusted.
control.question: What would a failed urlfetch on a fleet machine tell you about the courses that came before this one?

checklist: I recorded the template change that granted SBD Fleet Computers Enroll and Autoenroll on SBD Computer Authentication.
I confirmed a pilot enrolled its machine certificate at policy refresh with no manual request.
I saved certutil -verify -urlfetch output showing the chain and live AIA and CDP retrieval.

stepTitles: Add the NPS role to SBD-DHCP01
Add the RADIUS client and network policy
Set VLAN 90 and enable monitor mode
Audit NPS, then prove the pilots authenticate
nac.mistake: Enforcing 802.1X now instead of starting in monitor mode. The other 47 PCs have no machine certificate until they join, so enforcement would strand them in VLAN 90, with no route to a domain controller.
nac.network: NPS now runs beside DHCP on SBD-DHCP01. The pilots authenticate with EAP-TLS at their VLAN 80 ports in monitor mode, and NPS logs every grant and failure for the existing event subscription.

control.name: Device Identification and Authentication
control.body: 802.1X with EAP-TLS identifies each device by the machine certificate it enrolled before a port admits it. Monitor mode proves the configuration and logs every result before enforcement begins.
control.question: Which devices would fail authentication today, and what would happen to each one once enforcement is on?

checklist: I added the NPS role to SBD-DHCP01 with an SBD Server Authentication certificate from the issuing CA, admitted Domain Computers in the network policy, and turned on NPS auditing.
I confirmed each pilot authenticated with EAP-TLS and NPS logged event 6272.
I confirmed a failed attempt was logged but still forwarded on VLAN 80, and I added register row F20.

stepTitles: Roll out the remaining waves in monitor mode
Reconcile enrollment, then retire SBD-TEST80
Switch the ports to enforcement and test both ways
Define the sample and run the full check set
Write the sample failure rule
Enrol the fleet in event collection
scale.mistake: Switching the ports to enforcement before reconciling enrollment. Any PC that missed its certificate lands in VLAN 90, with no route to a domain controller, and cannot enroll from there.
scale.network: All fifty PCs now lease, join, enroll, and authenticate, and each forwards its security events to SBD-SYSLOG01 through SBD Event Sources. With enforcement on, an unenrolled device lands in quarantine VLAN 90, which has no routes.

control.name: Control Assessments
control.body: A defined sample, the pilot’s full check set, and a failure rule written before the checks run make the fleet’s proof repeatable. The enforcement test adds a negative result: an unenrolled device is quarantined.
control.question: Why must the sample and its failure rule be written down before any sampled host is checked?

checklist: I reconciled issued certificates and NPS grants against the fifty computer objects before enforcing.
I confirmed an enrolled PC still authenticated and an unenrolled test laptop landed in VLAN 90.
I wrote the sample definition and its failure rule before running the checks, and recorded each result.

stepTitles: Baseline the sample from SBD-ADMIN-PC01’s SCC copy
Rescan the infrastructure this course changed
Assemble the fleet inventory
Write the handoff to courses 1.14 and 1.15
scan.mistake: Scanning the endpoints with the Windows Server benchmark because it is already loaded. The fleet has its own Windows client STIG benchmark in the same DISA package; the wrong one measures the wrong standard.
scan.network: The finished fleet’s steady paths are shown: leases and 802.1X admission at SBD-DHCP01, domain services on the domain controller, certificates from SBD-SUBCA01, and events to SBD-SYSLOG01. SBD-ADMIN-PC01 scans the sample over remote management; the domain controllers, issuing CA and SBD-DHCP01 are rescanned.

control.name: System Component Inventory
control.body: The fleet inventory names each endpoint with its image ancestry, certificate thumbprint, and sample status. Course 1.15 makes it a source of SBD-MGMT01’s living inventory.
control.question: Which inventory fields would reveal a PC that had been rebuilt from a different image?

checklist: I checked the SCC installer course 1.8 kept on SBD-ADMIN-PC01 against its recorded hash before scanning the sample.
I baselined the lesson 6 sample with the Windows client STIG benchmark, removed SCC afterwards, and rescanned the controllers, issuing CA and SBD-DHCP01.
I filed the fleet inventory and a handoff note naming updates for course 1.14 and the inventory for course 1.15.
